title: Bayan Muna and multisectoral groups protest charter change at the House of Representatives
location: House of Representatives, Philippines (specific locality not stated in reviewed text)
organizer: Bayan Muna and multisectoral groups (as reported)
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Two opened contemporaneous reports establish a public protest but provide no attendee count; the group description alone does not establish 50 participants.

title.summary: Both contemporary reports identify a protest at the House against charter change.

organizer.summary: S005 names Bayan Muna; S006 describes multisectoral groups without naming the organizer.

demands.summary: The reports describe opposition to charter change, a domestic political-process issue; S005 also reports a call to prioritize COVID-19 response.

participants_original.summary: Neither opened body gives an attendance estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Public protest is reported, but the sources do not establish that at least 50 people assembled.

end_date.summary: Neither report establishes physical departure or dissolution; end remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: No reviewed statement establishes whether protesters used violence; unknown.

state_response.summary: No reviewed statement documents any of the seven state response dimensions; each remains unknown, not no_explicit.

scope.summary: The reviewed reports identify a single House gathering; no additional site is established. Scope is provisionally local.

state_response.accommodation.summary: No reviewed statement documents this response dimension; each remains unknown, not no_explicit.

state_response.arrests.summary: No reviewed statement documents this response dimension; each remains unknown, not no_explicit.

state_response.ignore.summary: No reviewed statement documents this response dimension; each remains unknown, not no_explicit.

state_response.killings.summary: No reviewed statement documents this response dimension; each remains unknown, not no_explicit.

state_response.shootings.summary: No reviewed statement documents this response dimension; each remains unknown, not no_explicit.

S005 has an apparent 2020 photo-caption typo, but the article body and S006 date the protest to Jan. 13, 2021. State target is the government’s charter-change deliberation; threshold and physical end are unverified. Opened secondary timeline S001 cites a Jan. 13 News5 post and describes students/youth at the House against Cha-Cha; the linked post failed Cache miss and is not independent open evidence. open_questions: How many people were physically present?
Was this the same gathering described by the secondary timeline as a student rally, or a separate action?

title: KMP Cebu-led protest marking Mendiola Massacre anniversary
organizer: Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) Cebu chapter with other progressive groups
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. The contemporary report identifies several sectors and a protest but gives no attendee estimate. The 10,000 peasants mentioned by the Commission on Human Rights refer to the 1987 Mendiola Massacre, not this 2021 gathering.

title.summary: Contemporary report identifies a KMP Cebu-led protest marking the massacre anniversary.

start_date.summary: Report states the protest took place Friday, January 22, 2021.

location.summary: Report locates the action on Colon Street in Cebu.

scope.summary: The reported gathering is on one street in Cebu; no coordinated multi-city action is established by this source.

organizer.summary: Report identifies the KMP Cebu chapter as lead organizer with progressive groups; farmers, workers and youth participated.

demands.summary: Report describes demands/issues involving agrarian reform, land conversion and displacement, human-rights abuses, government aid, and repeal of the Anti-Terrorism Act.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Several sectors are named, but no count or clear qualitative size establishes 50 or more.

end_date.summary: The article says police interrupted midway through the program but gives no departure or dissolution time.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence is described; silence does not establish no_explicit.

state_response.summary: Police reportedly blocked the group and sounded a siren to disrupt participants midway through the program. This may be an effort to disrupt/disperse, but the text does not say police moved participants or ended the assembly; crowd_dispersal therefore remains unknown. No arrests, beatings, killings, shootings, accommodation, or explicit ignoring are reported.

state_response.accommodation.summary: S017 does not establish this response dimension. The reported obstruction/siren is not enough to code another dimension; unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: S017 does not establish this response dimension. The reported obstruction/siren is not enough to code another dimension; unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: S017 does not establish this response dimension. The reported obstruction/siren is not enough to code another dimension; unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: S017 reports a police blockade and siren used to disrupt the program midway through, but does not clearly say the crowd was moved, prevented from assembling, or dispersed; unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: S017 does not establish this response dimension. The reported obstruction/siren is not enough to code another dimension; unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: S017 does not establish this response dimension. The reported obstruction/siren is not enough to code another dimension; unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: S017 does not establish this response dimension. The reported obstruction/siren is not enough to code another dimension; unknown.

notes: Do not transfer the CHR statement’s historical 1987 figures (10,000 participants and 13 deaths) to this 2021 protest. The reported police obstruction is a state-response lead but does not yet establish the exact dispersal action. The anniversary may have separate actions elsewhere; no cross-city fusion is assumed.
open_questions: Was the crowd at least 50?
Did police action move or break up the crowd, or did the program continue?
How did the gathering physically end?
Were there distinct 2021 anniversary marches in Manila or other cities?

scope: local Manila action; organizer announced a nationally coordinated mobilization
organizer: Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas (KMP) with other militant/peasant groups
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. Occurrence is reported by RMN and Philstar, but neither reports a participant count or clear qualitative size. The historical 1987 crowd of about 10,000 is not this event.

location.summary: RMN describes procession from UST on España Boulevard to Mendiola; Philstar says near Malacañang.

notes: This Manila action and the KMP Cebu Colon Street action (E003) share a national organizer, date and anniversary; KMP announced national coordination, but no source explicitly links Cebu to the observed Manila march. KMP’s Jan. 20 organizer report (S032) said KASAMA-TK planned to join this Jan. 22 march; the separately reported Jan. 20 caravan E006 is not merged with E004. Potential continuation/overlap with the Jan. 20–21 KASAMA-TK caravan E006: S032/S034 say the group planned to join the Jan. 22 Mendiola march from its CHR camp, and S020/S021 report the Manila march. title: KASAMA-TK Southern Luzon farmers’ multi-day protest caravan
location: Jan. 20: Camp Aguinaldo, DILG and Philippine Coconut Authority in Quezon City; Jan. 21: Department of Agrarian Reform and camp at the Commission on Human Rights (site sequence/route and CHR locality not specified)
scope: Multi-day Southern Luzon farmers’ protest caravan; Jan. 20 and Jan. 21 are explicitly described as successive days. Possible relation to the Jan. 22 Mendiola march is unresolved.
organizer: Katipunan ng mga Samahang Magsasaka sa Timog Katagalugan (KASAMA-TK), with Southern Tagalog farmers and KMP networks
participants_original: More than a hundred farmers from Southern Tagalog (KMP organizer report)
threshold_50_evidence: The KMP organizer-origin account says more than a hundred farmers took part in the Jan. 20 caravan, directly above the 50-person threshold. It gives no separate Jan. 21 or Jan. 22 count; source dependence is retained. The event’s relationship to the Jan. 22 Manila march must be reviewed before distinct-event counting.

title.summary: KMP’s contemporary report identifies the Southern Tagalog farmers’ Jan. 20 protest caravan to Quezon City.

start_date.summary: The organizer report is dated Jan. 20, 2021 and says the caravan and quick protest activities occurred that day.

location.summary: S032 identifies quick actions at Camp Aguinaldo and DILG and a protest outside the Philippine Coconut Authority on Jan. 20. S034 identifies the next day’s farmers at DAR and a camp at CHR; it does not state that the planned DA and DENR actions occurred.

scope.summary: S034 explicitly calls Jan. 21 the second day of the Jan. 20 caravan. S032 says the group planned to join the Jan. 22 march; S034 says the group was camped at CHR and planned to march to Mendiola the next day. S020/S021 confirm a Jan. 22 Manila march but do not establish that the whole march was the same physical episode; pending unit review.

organizer.summary: KMP says KASAMA-TK, its Southern Tagalog regional chapter, led the delegation. S034 identifies KASAMA-TK’s chair as the source for the Jan. 21 caravan account.

demands.summary: KMP describes demands to end militarization, peasant killings and human-rights violations attributed to state forces, alongside disputes over land grabbing and local land cases; these target state conduct/policy.

participants_original.summary: S032 reports more than a hundred farmers for the Jan. 20 caravan. S034 describes the next day’s delegation but gives no separate count; no count is transferred to later days.

participants_min.summary: S032 directly implies at least 101 participants for the Jan. 20 caravan from “more than a hundred”; S034 provides no separate Jan. 21 lower bound.

participants_max.summary: Neither report provides an upper bound.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The organizer reports more than 100 farmers, directly exceeding 50; source dependence is retained for review.

end_date.summary: S034 says a Jan. 22 Mendiola march was planned from the CHR camp; S020/S021 report the Manila march, but do not establish whether this caravan ended there or when participants physically departed. End remains unknown pending unit review.

protester_violence.summary: The report discusses prior killings and alleged state abuses, not violence by protesters during this caravan; protester violence is unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: S034 reports the planned face-to-face dialogue with DAR was canceled and an online schedule was proposed, but does not report an actual hearing or completed meeting. Whether this amounts to accommodation remains unknown.

state_response.arrests.summary: S032/S034 do not establish this response dimension during the caravan; unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: S032/S034 do not establish this response dimension during the caravan; unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: S032/S034 do not establish this response dimension during the caravan; unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: S034 reports a canceled face-to-face dialogue and proposed online scheduling; this does not establish a deliberate refusal/ignoring of all demands. Unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: S032/S034 discuss historical/contextual peasant killings but do not report state killings in response to this caravan. Event-specific status remains unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: S032/S034 do not establish this response dimension during the caravan; unknown.

state_response.summary: S034 reports that a planned face-to-face dialogue with DAR was canceled at the last minute and the agency asked to schedule an online meeting. The account does not report a completed dialogue, explicit refusal of all contact, or another coded response category; accommodation and ignore remain unknown. All other state-response dimensions are also unknown.

notes: The source says participants held quick actions at Camp Aguinaldo and DILG, also protested at the Philippine Coconut Authority, and planned similar Jan. 21 actions at DA, DAR and DENR. The earlier standalone Jan. 21 lead is preserved as E007 in excluded.json as superseded: S034 confirms Jan. 21 as the second day and reports activity at DAR, while whether planned actions at DA and DENR occurred remains unresolved. It also says the group planned to join the separately reported Jan. 22 Mendiola march (E004); this link does not merge the dates. Prior 2016–2020 killings/land disputes are motivating context, not event response. S034 reports farmers from at least 20 landholdings going to DAR and camping at CHR. It says a planned face-to-face dialogue with the DAR Secretary was canceled in favor of an online schedule; no completed hearing or other accommodation is established. A Jan. 22 Mendiola march is linked by the group’s plans and later reporting, but the episode boundary remains unresolved. E006 and E004 are retained separately with a shared tentative episode key and pending_unit; do not count them as distinct approved events until review.
open_questions: Does the Jan. 20–21 caravan physically continue into the Jan. 22 Mendiola march reported in E004, or is E004 a broader separate gathering?
Were the planned Jan. 21 actions at DA and DENR held, in addition to the reported presence at DAR?
Was there a completed meeting, online or otherwise, with DAR officials?
What were the Jan. 21 and Jan. 22 attendance, site sequence, end time and state responses?
Can independent contemporary reporting corroborate the organizer’s Jan. 20 count and the Jan. 21 actions?
